Composing a smooth test with it gives a smooth test (SmoothGradient.Test.compSmoothed) whose gradient norm is pointwise not larger, hence with energy at most that of the test, and whose L^2 class converges to the contracted class. lem:conditional-fiber-form.note: Proved in Lean on 2026-09-11. The route is the jump representation energyAt_eq_jump_div: on a nondegenerate fiber the normalized variance is the squared jump integral against the two-point measure (kappa b) x (kappa b) divided by 2 Var(id), by the new two-point variance identity Probability.two_mul_evariance_eq_lintegral_prod (Probability/TwoPointVariance.lean, valid in [0, infinity] without square integrability). Symmetry and reversibility are read as this representation and the swap invariance twoPointMeasure_swap. Closedness pushes an almost-everywhere convergent subsequence (TendstoInMeasure.exists_seq_tendsto_ae) through the joint law and the disintegration (Measure.ae_ae_of_ae_compProd) and applies Fatou (lintegral_liminf_le) on the two-point space and on the base law; Lipschitz tests have energy at most d L^2 (energy_le_of_lipschitzWith), so the smooth compactly supported core (WeightedGradient.dense_smoothCore) lies in the finite domain. The line slice t -> f(z + t theta) has local slope |<theta, grad f>| at Rademacher points (HasFDerivAt.comp_hasDerivAt, HasDerivAt.hasGradientAt, the existing apply_eq_norm_gradient); the Rademacher null set and square integrability pass through the joint law and Measure.ae_ae_of_ae_compProd; Measure.lintegral_compProd, lintegral_map with reconstruct_coordinates, lintegral_prod_symm and the frame identity (ofReal_integral_eq_lintegral_ofReal) give kappa times the gradient energy, identified with the local-slope energy by energy_eq_lintegral_gradient. cor:conditional-fiber-twelve-bound.note: Proved in Lean on 2026-09-11 and registered on 2026-09-12. Three pieces of new infrastructure close the gaps recorded on 2026-09-11. (1) Probability/Line/BrunnMinkowski.lean proves compact one-dimensional Brunn-Minkowski (translate K by inf L and L by sup K inside K + L; the two translates meet in a single point, so measure_union_add_inter with translation invariance gives vol K + vol L <= vol (K + L)), its inner-regular convex-combination form, and the fully general one-dimensional Prekopa-Leindler inequality (layer cake lintegral_eq_lintegral_meas_lt, the level-set inclusion t {f > s} + (1-t) {g > s} subset {h > s}, normalization of both factors to supremum one by homogeneity, truncation with monotone convergence for unbounded factors, and a two-term ENNReal AM-GM proved from NNReal.geom_mean_le_arith_mean2_weighted). KLS/LogConcave/Line/OfDensity.lean applies it to indicator multiples of a Borell density and gives LineDensity.logConcave, the converse of the existing LogConcave.exists_lineDensity. (2) Probability/Line/Haar.lean builds the linear equivalence (R theta)-perp x R = E, (z, s) -> z + s theta, and proves exists_lintegral_line: for a unit theta there is a positive finite c with c * integral G dm = double integral of G(z + s theta) against addHaar and volume (ContinuousLinearEquiv.isAddHaarMeasure_map, Measure.isAddLeftInvariant_eq_smul, addHaarScalarFactor_pos_of_isAddHaarMeasure); c depends on theta and is never evaluated, and the proof never needs measurability of theta -> c. (3) KLS/ConditionalFiber/SliceKernel.lean defines sliceMass, SliceGood, sliceDensity and the Markov kernel sliceKernel (Kernel.withDensity of the normalized line density on the good set, Kernel.piecewise with a Dirac law elsewhere) and proves compProd_baseLaw_sliceKernel (baseLaw ⊗ₘ sliceKernel = jointLaw) by reducing both sides, for each fixed direction, to the same iterated integral through exists_lintegral_line; finiteness of the slice mass almost everywhere is the case G = 1 of that identity. ae_sliceKernel_eq is then ProbabilityTheory.eq_condKernel_of_measure_eq_compProd. Assembly: absolute continuity gives full affine support (affineSupport_eq_top_of_absolutelyContinuous, made public in EnergyComparison.lean without a type change) and hence a Borell density; on a good base point the normalized line density is a Borell density of the slice kernel (upper semicontinuity by UpperSemicontinuous.comp and Continuous.comp_upperSemicontinuous, log-concavity along the affine reconstruction map), so LineDensity.logConcave applies; the remaining base points carry a Dirac law and KLS.logConcave_dirac covers them, so no exceptional set is discarded.
